gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured wired delay for any picked soundbar: the Sony HT-S100F measures 62 ms over HDMI ARC and 70 ms over optical (Gadget Review). That is 1.5–1.7 film frames at 24 fps, under the ITU-R BT.1359 lip-sync detectability limit of 125 ms audio lag. The portable pick, Bose SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen), has no AUX input, and its measured 7 h 03 min battery covers only 2 full 3-hour TV evenings per charge.
standout_why: I compared against geekchamp.com (Nov 2026), itechguides.com's cited connection guide, and thegoodatheist.net. I could not read itechguides.com's main list (fetch timed out) or What Hi-Fi's cited page (it came back truncated). Geekchamp gives only PCWorld's general 'up to about 150 ms' for Bluetooth and says plainly that it has no per-product measurement. The itechguides guide gives no millisecond figures at all. Thegoodatheist gives general ranges ('100-200ms' Bluetooth, ARC/optical 'under 40ms') and no measurement for any model. The HT-S100F's measured 62/70 ms contradicts that 'under 40ms' claim. None of the pages turns a delay into frames or compares it with a lip-sync threshold. None gives evenings per charge for a portable speaker used with a TV, and none flags that the Flex has no wired input.
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's soundbar-over-portable advice and makes it measurable. On the budget pick (HT-S100F), connecting by cable keeps the delay at 1.5–1.7 frames, inside the ITU detectability limit. Portable speakers like the Bose Flex 2 have no AUX input, so they must use the TV's Bluetooth output (if the TV has one), and they need charging every 2 evenings. The page should recommend the cable (ARC) route on the soundbar, and treat a portable speaker as a second option only for TVs with Bluetooth audio out.

findings.label: Measured audio delay, HDMI ARC, in 24 fps frames
findings.source_title: Sony HT-S100F Review (Gadget Review, Nikshep Myle, updated 2023-12-20)
findings.note: 62 ms ÷ 41.7 ms per frame (1000/24) = 1.49 frames. The page quotes 'measuring 62ms via ARC and 70ms via Optical' but does not describe the test procedure.

findings.label: Measured audio delay, optical, in 24 fps frames
findings.source_title: Sony HT-S100F Review (Gadget Review, Nikshep Myle, updated 2023-12-20)

findings.label: Margin under the ITU-R BT.1359 detectability limit for audio lag (ARC)
findings.value: 63 ms of margin (62 ms vs 125 ms)
findings.note: 125 − 62 = 63 ms. Wikipedia: detectability is '45 ms lead to 125 ms lag'. The ITU PDF downloaded but I could not extract its text, so this is from a secondary source. If the TV adds its own delay, that uses up part of the margin.

findings.label: Stricter broadcast lip-sync limit (ATSC IS-191), as a frame budget
findings.note: 45 ÷ 41.7 = 1.08 frames. The HT-S100F's 62 ms ARC delay exceeds this stricter limit but stays under the ITU detectability limit.

findings.label: TV evenings per charge at 3 h per evening (measured runtime)
findings.source_title: Bose SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen) review (SoundGuys, Dave Carr, 2025-06-19)
findings.note: 7.05 h ÷ 3 h = 2.35, so 2 full evenings. Bose's 12 h claim ÷ 3 = 4 evenings. SoundGuys measured with its standard battery test.

findings.label: Wired input / codecs
findings.value: No AUX input; SBC and AAC, plus aptX on Snapdragon Sound Android phones
findings.source_title: Bose SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen) review (SoundGuys, Dave Carr, 2025-06-19)
findings.note: With no AUX input, a TV can only connect over Bluetooth, so the TV must support Bluetooth audio output.
